steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) has been an active research topic for the last two decades. One major byproduct of this is that many different scene representations have been investigated, either to push the tracking performance and mapping capabilities or to adapt SLAM for more complex downstream tasks like path planning or semantic understanding. Earlier works focus on tracking and use scene representations like feature point clouds, surfels, depth maps, or implicit representations. Later works focus more on how good and dense the map is. Then powerful neural scene representations like neural radiance fields appeared, which allow high fidelity view-synthesis, and a lot of dense neural SLAM methods have been developed quickly. These methods gave impressive gains in the quality of the scene representation, but they are still limited to small synthetic scenes and their re-rendering results are far from photo-realistic.

Recently a new scene representation based on Gaussian splatting has been shown to give rendering performance on par with NeRFs while being an order of magnitude faster in rendering and optimization. Also, this representation is directly interpretable and can be manipulated directly, which is useful for many downstream tasks. Because of these advantages, Gaussian splatting is a good fit for an online SLAM system with real-time demands and it opens the door to photo-realistic dense SLAM.

- Gaussian-SLAM
  - dense RGBD SLAM with 3D Gaussians: mapping, tracking, photo-realistic re-rendering at interactive runtimes
  - example in Fig. 1
  - contributions: SOTA rendering on real-world scenes; Gaussian splatting extension for geometry, single camera; online optimization with sub-maps, seeding and optimization strategies; frame-to-model tracker (photometric + geometric error)
  - code and data public

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) has been an active research topic for the last two decades. One major byproduct of this is that many different scene representations have been investigated, either to push the tracking performance and mapping capabilities or to adapt SLAM for more complex downstream tasks like path planning or semantic understanding. Earlier works focus on tracking and use scene representations like feature point clouds, surfels, depth maps, or implicit representations. Later works focus more on how good and dense the map is. Then powerful neural scene representations like neural radiance fields appeared, which allow high fidelity view-synthesis, and a lot of dense neural SLAM methods have been developed quickly. These methods gave impressive gains in the quality of the scene representation, but they are still limited to small synthetic scenes and their re-rendering results are far from photo-realistic.

Recently a new scene representation based on Gaussian splatting has been shown to give rendering performance on par with NeRFs while being an order of magnitude faster in rendering and optimization. Also, this representation is directly interpretable and can be manipulated directly, which is useful for many downstream tasks. Because of these advantages, Gaussian splatting is a good fit for an online SLAM system with real-time demands and it opens the door to photo-realistic dense SLAM.

In this paper we introduce Gaussian-SLAM, which is a dense RGBD SLAM system that uses 3D Gaussians to build a scene representation that allows mapping, tracking, and photo-realistic re-rendering at interactive runtimes. Fig. 1 shows an example of the high-fidelity rendering output of Gaussian-SLAM. Our contributions are:

- A dense RGBD SLAM approach using 3D Gaussians to build a scene representation which gives SOTA rendering results on real-world scenes.

- An extension of Gaussian splatting that encodes geometry better and allows reconstruction beyond radiance fields with a single camera.

- An online optimization method for Gaussian splats which processes the map as sub-maps and introduces efficient seeding and optimization strategies.

- A frame-to-model tracker with the Gaussian splatting scene representation using photometric and geometric error minimization.

We will make all source code and data publicly available.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) has been an active research topic for the past two decades [1,2]. A major byproduct of this journey is the investigation of various scene representations, either to push tracking performance and mapping capabilities or to adapt SLAM for more complex downstream tasks like path planning or semantic understanding. Specifically, earlier works focus on tracking using scene representations like feature point clouds [3,4,5], surfels [6,7], depth maps [8,9], or implicit representations [10,11,12]. Later works focus more on map quality and density. With the advent of powerful neural scene representations like neural radiance fields [13] that allow for high fidelity view-synthesis, a rapidly growing body of dense neural SLAM methods [14,15,16,17,18,19,20,21] has been developed. Despite their impressive gains in scene representation quality, these methods remain limited to small synthetic scenes, and their re-rendering results are far from photo-realistic.

Recently, a novel scene representation based on Gaussian splatting [22] has been shown to deliver rendering performance on par with NeRFs while being an order of magnitude faster in rendering and optimization. Moreover, this representation is directly interpretable and can be directly manipulated, which is desirable for many downstream tasks. With these advantages, Gaussian splatting lends itself to an online SLAM system with real-time demands and opens the door to photo-realistic dense SLAM.

In this paper, we introduce Gaussian-SLAM, a dense RGBD SLAM system that uses 3D Gaussians to build a scene representation allowing for mapping, tracking, and photo-realistic re-rendering at interactive runtimes. An example of Gaussian-SLAM's high-fidelity rendering output is shown in Fig. 1. In summary, our contributions include:

- A dense RGBD SLAM approach that uses 3D Gaussians to construct a scene representation allowing SOTA rendering results on real-world scenes.

- An extension of Gaussian splatting that better encodes geometry and allows reconstruction beyond radiance fields in a single-camera setup.

- An online optimization method for Gaussian splats that processes the map as sub-maps and introduces efficient seeding and optimization strategies.

- A frame-to-model tracker with the Gaussian splatting scene representation via photometric and geometric error minimization.

All source code and data will be made publicly available.
